clips.text: One question opens up a whole different kind of afternoon: not what should I see, but what's actually happening. The plaza, the local market, a neighbourhood event — the answer changes week to week, and that's exactly the point.
¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?
Turn the question back around. This is the one that gets you invited into someone's actual plan instead of a tourist itinerary.
Ask what's happening in the plaza this weekend. Speak now.
¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?
Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.
A mercado sobre ruedas — a market that sets up on a street for one day and moves on — is a completely different rhythm from a fixed tourist market. Ask to go along, not just for directions.
Ask if you can come along with them. Speak now.
¿Puedo ir con ustedes?
Claro, nos vemos a las diez.
Once you're there, you're not performing tourism. You're just at the market with everyone else, so the useful sentence is the same one anyone would use.
Ask the price of something at a stall, like any other customer. Speak now.
¿Cuánto cuesta esto?
¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana? ¿Puedo ir con ustedes?

I09 complete. ¿Hay algo en la plaza? finds out what's actually happening. ¿Puedo ir con ustedes? turns a plan into an invitation. Once you're there, you're just a customer, not a spectator — cuánto cuesta esto works exactly the same way it does everywhere else.
